records.tutor: Hi, I'm glad you could make it today. To start things off, please tell me a bit about yourself and your experience.

records.learner: Hi Nathalie, nice to meet you. I'm Nicolás, a full-stack developer based in Córdoba, Argentina, and I'm in Colombia until mid-December, so I'm on Eastern time right now. I've been writing code for six years, five of them shipping React and TypeScript, and the closest thing to your project is Valley of Guardians, a live web game with more than ten thousand users, where I ran the full stack on Supabase, including payments that were only credited after server-side verification. Right now I'm also the sole front-end developer at Doubland, a live AI simulation built with Next.js.
records.planted_point: Said 'a full stack on Supabase' but mangled as 'full stack on Superbase' — should be 'Supabase'; also left out that I work alone with no agency, and left out the ten thousand users figure from the prepared introduction.
records.tutor: Thank you for that background. Now, let's talk about security. How do you protect the comic panels from being copied?

judge.note: The coach moves to a new bank question on panel protection without correcting the 'Superbase' mangling or noting the missing 'works alone' and user-count points.

records.learner: Sure. The panels live in a private bucket, so storage rules block direct reads for every user. The only way to get an image is through our API route, which checks the session and whether the user has access to that chapter. If yes, the server signs the file path with a 120-second expiry and returns it with Cache-Control: no-store, so nothing caches it. The reader asks for links panel by panel as you scroll, and every two minutes the global timer rotates the links, so a scraper only ever holds a few that die quickly.
records.planted_point: Said 'every two minutes the global timer rotates the links' as if a global timer rotates all links at once, instead of each signed URL expiring 120 seconds after it is signed.
records.tutor: Feedback: You said the links expire every two minutes from a global timer; each link expires 120 seconds after it is signed. What happens if someone takes a screenshot of the panel while the link is active?

answer_errors: Says a global timer rotates the links every two minutes, instead of each signed URL expiring 120 seconds after it is signed.
answer_missing: The browser message never unlocks anything / access is granted only by server-side verification
A screenshot or phone photo can't be stopped by any website; a watermark with the reader's ID helps later (out of scope)
judge.note: The coach correctly fixes the global-timer misconception and follows up on the candidate's own answer with a screenshot what-if.

records.learner: Right, so basically we can't stop a screenshot, you know? We do the front-end blocking, like right-click and shortcuts, so the casual user can't save the image easily. But if someone really wants to take a photo or screenshot, we can't prevent that, so yeah, that's something we can't fully control. We just make it harder for the normal user, something like that.
records.planted_point: The specific mechanism to address screenshots: a watermark with the reader's ID to make leaks traceable, which is the actual mitigation mentioned in the lesson.
records.tutor: Feedback: the part about front-end limitations is right. Now, how do you know a payment confirmed in the browser is really valid?

answer_missing: a watermark with the reader's ID makes leaks traceable (the actual mitigation for screenshots)
the real protection is on the server, with the 120-second signed links
the front-end blocking is only a brake for the casual user, not security
judge.note: The coach's feedback only affirms the front-end limitation and moves to a new bank question, never naming the watermark mitigation or the server-side protection the candidate omitted.

records.learner: Good question. The postMessage from the Centrobill iframe only refreshes the UI, it never unlocks anything by itself, because anyone can fake a message from the console. The real unlock happens when Centrobill's server sends the postback to our Next.js route, we verify the payment there, and then we write the access row in Supabase. So when the iframe says paid, we check the signature in the postMessage listener before we unlock the chapter.
records.planted_point: Says the signature is checked in the postMessage listener and that this unlocks the chapter; correct version: the browser message only refreshes the UI, and access is granted when the server verifies Centrobill's postback and writes the access row.
records.tutor: Feedback: You said we check the signature in the browser listener; the browser checks only origin and shape, while verification happens on the server postback. What if Centrobill takes two weeks to send the sandbox credentials?

answer_errors: Says the signature is checked in the postMessage listener before unlocking the chapter; per the lesson the browser listener only checks event.origin and message shape, and the browser message never unlocks anything — access is granted only when the server verifies Centrobill's postback and writes the access row.
answer_missing: The browser message never unlocks anything by itself — it only tells the screen to check again
While waiting for the postback the screen shows 'confirming your payment' for a second or two
judge.note: The coach correctly corrects the planted error (signature checked in the browser listener) but then asks an unexpected what-if about Centrobill sandbox credentials, which no prepared answer covers.

records.learner: Well, if the sandbox credentials come late, I'd keep working on the other parts of that week, you know, the iframe layout and the listener, and I'd mock the postback on our side so we can test the flow without them. But honestly, I haven't thought about it too much, I mean, I know week three is the creator side, with the upload portal and the moderation, and the pricing floors, something like that, and then the payments come after. So yeah, I guess we'd adjust the order a bit if it's really late.
records.planted_point: Missing the rest of the week-three items (AI scan flagging safe/adult content, auto-cropping into vertical panels) and the whole week-four payment items; only names upload portal and pricing floors vaguely.
records.tutor: Feedback: You said you would adjust the order; you must ask for credentials on day one because you need them by week three, and nothing is faked in production. Walk me through the six weeks; what is in each milestone?

answer_missing: the AI scan that flags safe or adult content
the week-four payment items (Centrobill iframe and postback, paywall at chapter four, 18-plus gate)
judge.note: The coach corrects the candidate's plan to mock the postback and asks for the six milestones, but does not name the missing week-three and week-four items.

records.learner: Sure. It's five weekly milestones plus a QA week, and every Wednesday the code is on your GitHub and on Vercel staging. Week one is the foundation: the full schema in Supabase, row-level security on every table, the 45/55 split, and the private buckets. Week two is protection: the 120-second signed links, the protected reader, and the Sunday leaderboard reset. Week three is the creator side: the upload portal, the AI scan that flags safe or adult content, auto-cropping into vertical panels, and the price floors. Week four is payments: the Centrobill iframe and postback, the paywall at chapter four, and the 18-plus gate. Week five is payouts and revenue: the Paxum payout ledger, the ad slots for non-paying readers, and the print-on-demand webhooks. Week six is only testing and polish, with sign-off on December 24th.
records.planted_point: nothing to correct: the coach should not invent an error
records.tutor: Feedback: perfect, your walkthrough of the milestones is exactly what I needed. Now, how does the Sunday leaderboard reset work, and what happens if it runs twice by mistake?

judge.note: The milestone walkthrough is complete and correct, and the coach praises it without inventing any error, then asks a question covered by the prepared reset answer.

records.learner: I use pg_cron inside Supabase, and it calls one SQL function that does everything in a single transaction: it copies the week's winners to an archive table and then sets the counters to zero. If something fails in the middle, nothing changes. And since I put a unique key on the week, if the job runs twice by mistake, the second run does nothing, so it's idempotent. Actually I also would store the votes per week, so the reset never deletes nothing and we keep the history for stats.
records.planted_point: 1) 'since I put a unique key' → 'because I put a unique key' (since + simple past is wrong; use because for cause, since for time). 2) 'never deletes nothing' → 'never deletes anything' (double negative). Also 'Actually' used for 'currently' is a false friend, but the two main ones are the since/because and the double negative.
records.tutor: Feedback: you said "never deletes nothing," say "never deletes anything." Everything else is correct. How will you handle the time zone change for the reset, since pg_cron runs in UTC and Chicago observes daylight saving time?

judge.note: The candidate's reset answer matches the lesson (single transaction, unique week key, per-week votes); the coach only corrects the double negative and moves to the time-zone question covered by the prepared answer.

records.learner: Right, so pg_cron works in UTC, but Chicago changes between summer and winter, so a fixed UTC hour would be off by one hour half the year. What I do is let the job check the local time in your time zone before it runs, so it always closes at Sunday 23:59 your time. And with the unique week key, even if it runs twice, the second run does nothing.
records.planted_point: The lesson's senior detail is that the job checks the client's local time before acting, plus the unique week key; here the learner mentions both, but omits that pg_cron fires on a UTC schedule and the local-time check is what makes the Sunday 23:59 boundary hold across daylight saving — actually the missing must-say is that the job runs on a fixed UTC trigger and the local-time check is the guard against the DST shift.
records.tutor: Feedback: all the details about handling the time zone change and idempotency are correct. Let's discuss finances. On a refund, what happens to the creator's fifty-five percent share?

answer_missing: the job runs on a fixed UTC trigger and the local-time check is the guard against the DST shift
judge.note: The coach praises the time-zone answer as fully correct although the learner never states that pg_cron fires on a fixed UTC schedule with the local-time check guarding the DST boundary, then asks an uncovered refund question.

records.learner: I think that's all I have time for. Can we wrap up?

Your English error correction was to say "never deletes anything" instead of "never deletes nothing." Your prepared answers were strong. Interview complete.
